subject: Dedicated deployment site binding and secure wipe schedule - Aurora Financial
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@aurorafin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: audits@aurorafin.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated deployment region binding and backup locality questions

Hi Ben,

Quick follow-up from our compliance review: before we execute the purchase order we need confirmation on two things for the Dedicated deployment you proposed.

1) Can you confirm that tenant data (including snapshots and backups) will remain physically within our chosen US region and will not replicate outside that region under normal operation?
2) We need a documented schedule and runbook for emergency and routine data wipes for tenant-scoped backups and any ephemeral caches. Our auditors are asking for an estimated time-to-wipe SLA and evidence artifacts you can provide after a wipe.

Appreciate a concise response we can circulate internally.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Compliance
Aurora Financial

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated deployment region binding and backup locality questions

Ben — draft technical summary below (summarized for Aurora):

- Region binding: Dedicated VPC nodes are pinned to the customer's selected cloud region. Persistent volumes and object storage used for tenant snapshots are configured with region-local buckets/volumes. Under normal operation there is no cross-region replication.

- Backups & snapshots: Automated snapshots are stored in the same region and retained per the retention policy. We only replicate out-of-region for DR in two scenarios: (a) when explicit cross-region DR is requested in the contract, or (b) when proactive capacity failover is triggered and customer has opted into geo-failover. Neither applies by default for Aurora.

- Wipe/runbook highlights:
  * Trigger: Customer SR or certified redwood ops task (we run tenant-scoped purge job).
  * Steps: disable new writes -> snapshot final state -> delete volumes -> scrub metadata indexes -> zero/cryptographic delete on attached volumes -> remove snapshots -> verify removal from object store.
  * Evidence: job run id, task logs (timestamped), list of removed snapshot IDs, object-store lifecycle logs, and ops ticket id.
  * Expected completion: typical dataset (<= 2TB) full purge completes in 2–6 hours; larger datasets scale linearly.

- Retention/soft-delete: We keep a short soft-delete window (default 24 hours) to prevent accidental full-loss; we can shorten to 0h if required contractually.

I've attached a checklist and a draft runbook we can share. Please review for compliance language.

Attachments: redwood-region-isolation-checklist.pdf (pdf), aurora-wipe-runbook-20261115.docx (docx), region-binding-assertion.csv (csv)

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@aurorafin.com>, audits@aurorafin.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:53:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment region binding and backup locality questions

Elena — thanks for the questions. Below is our client-ready summary and the artifacts we can provide as part of onboarding and compliance reviews. Please let me know if you need further detail or different artifact formats.

1) Region locality
- Confirmation: Tenant data (live volumes, snapshots, backups, and ephemeral caches) will remain in the selected US region by default.
- Exceptions: Cross-region replication will only occur if explicitly included in the contract (e.g., geo-DR) or in rare emergency failover scenarios when the customer has pre-authorized geo-failover.

2) Wipe & evidence
- Runbook: Attached (aurora-wipe-runbook-20261115.docx) — full step-by-step.
- Typical wipe timeline: 2–6 hours for up to 2TB, then linear scaling. We include a job run id and timestamped logs as evidence.
- Artifacts provided after a purge: job run id, list of deleted snapshot IDs, object-store deletion logs, and an ops ticket with full audit trail. We can provide hashed manifests for verification if required.

3) Options & customizations
- Reduce soft-delete window to 0 hours (contract change)
- On-demand notarized attestation report following a purge (one-off for an extra fee)
- Quarterly attestation export to your audit bucket (automated)

Next steps: if that matches your needs we will: (a) include the region-binding clause in the SOW, (b) attach the wipe runbook to the onboarding checklist, and (c) schedule a short operations handoff call to review the runbook with Aurora's ops/audit team.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: aurora-wipe-runbook-20261115.docx)
From: Elena Morales <elena@aurorafin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: audits@aurorafin.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment region binding and backup locality questions

Ben — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. A couple of quick clarifications:

- We will accept the default (no cross-region replication) and add geo-DR only if requested later.
- Please set soft-delete to 0 hours for our tenant as a contractual requirement.
- We'd like the notarized attestation option for the first scheduled purge after onboarding; please include pricing and lead time.

Can you get the SOW clause and the modified runbook (soft-delete=0) back to me by end-of-week? Once we have that we can finalize procurement and move to signature.

Thanks — will loop audits if we need further artifact formats.

Best,
Elena
Head of Compliance
Aurora Financial
